# astro CLI reference

<!-- Code generated by scripts/generate-cli-docs.mjs; DO NOT EDIT. -->

This reference is generated from the shipped Cobra command tree. The CLI uses the same public API as the dashboard; use `astro docs` to locate or print the live OpenAPI document.

## `astro`

```text
astro is the command-line client for the Astronomer multi-cluster
management plane.

Run "astro login" first to authenticate. Then explore:

  astro cluster list                 # all managed clusters
  astro delivery source list         # Continuous Delivery sources
  astro delivery target preview      # authoritative placement preview
  astro cluster-agent list           # Cluster Agent health
  astro cluster manifest <id>        # download agent install YAML
  astro cluster self-test <id>       # run agent health checks
  astro cluster delete <id>          # decommission a cluster
  astro cluster shell <id>           # interactive kubectl session
  astro k8s <id> get pods -A         # kubectl-equivalent passthrough
  astro docs                         # open the live API reference

The CLI talks to the same REST API the dashboard uses (see the
OpenAPI spec at <server>/api/v1/openapi.yaml). Any operation the
dashboard can perform, this CLI can — and vice versa.

Usage:
  astro [command]

Available Commands:
  admin         Platform administration (SMTP, webhooks, vault, network policies, keys)
  audit         Audit logs, activity feed, alerting, API tools, and extensions
  backup        Manage backups, schedules, and storage configuration
  catalog       Browse and manage the Helm catalog (charts, repositories, installs, operations)
  cluster       Manage clusters
  cluster-agent Inspect and upgrade managed Cluster Agents
  completion    Generate shell completion script
  config        Inspect and edit the CLI config (~/.config/astronomer/config.yaml)
  delivery      Manage Continuous Delivery sources, bundles, targets, rollouts, and deployments
  docs          Show where to find the OpenAPI spec / Swagger UI
  help          Help about any command
  k8s           Proxy a Kubernetes API request through the cluster's agent tunnel
  login         Authenticate to an Astronomer server
  logout        Clear the locally-stored auth token
  monitoring    Cluster monitoring: metrics, health, conditions, vulnerabilities, events, service mesh
  nodes         Inspect and manage cluster nodes
  projects      Manage projects (cluster-scoped namespace policy containers)
  rbac          Manage RBAC roles, bindings, and permissions
  settings      Manage platform settings
  users         Manage users
  whoami        Show the currently-authenticated user
  workloads     Inspect and act on cluster workloads (deployments, statefulsets, jobs, ...)

Flags:
  -h, --help            help for astro
      --json            alias for --output json (deprecated)
  -o, --output string   output format: table|json|yaml (default "table")
      --server string   Astronomer server URL (overrides ~/.config/astronomer/config.yaml)
      --token string    API bearer token (overrides stored JWT; ASTRO_API_TOKEN also honored)
  -v, --version         version for astro

Use "astro [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

## `astro admin`

```text
Administer platform-wide settings as an operator.

These commands target the /api/v1/admin/* endpoints and require an
admin-scoped token. Each subcommand prints its result in the format
selected by the global -o/--output flag (table|json|yaml).

Usage:
  astro admin [command]

Available Commands:
  agents                   Inspect fleet agent administration posture
  backup-drill             Run / report the backup restore drill
  emails                   Inspect the platform email outbox
  key-status               Show encryption/JWT key counts and as-of timestamp
  network-policy-templates Manage network policy templates
  shell-sessions           Inspect cluster shell sessions
  smtp                     Inspect and manage platform SMTP settings
  vault                    Manage Vault connections
  webhook                  Inspect webhook deliveries
  webhooks                 Manage webhook subscriptions

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for admin

Global Flags:
      --json            alias for --output json (deprecated)
  -o, --output string   output format: table|json|yaml (default "table")
      --server string   Astronomer server URL (overrides ~/.config/astronomer/config.yaml)
      --token string    API bearer token (overrides stored JWT; ASTRO_API_TOKEN also honored)

Use "astro admin [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

## `astro admin smtp update`

```text
Update the platform SMTP settings.

Pass the new settings as JSON via --data. Send "password":"<encrypted>"
to keep the stored password, or "" to clear it.

  astro admin smtp update --data '{"enabled":true,"host":"smtp.example.com","port":587}'

Usage:
  astro admin smtp update [flags]

Flags:
      --data string   JSON body (inline, @file, or - for stdin)
  -h, --help          help for update
```

## `astro cluster create`

```text
create posts to /api/v1/clusters/ and prints the new cluster's
ID + registration phase. The next steps for the operator:

  astro cluster manifest <id> | kubectl --context=<target> apply --server-side --field-manager=astronomer-bootstrap -f -

That installs the agent into the target cluster, which then connects
back. Run "astro cluster get <id>" to watch the registration phase
advance.

Usage:
  astro cluster create <name> [flags]
```

```text

    source <(astro completion bash)

  Zsh:
    source <(astro completion zsh)
    # ensure 'autoload -U compinit; compinit' has run
```

## `astro config`

```text
config reads and writes the on-disk CLI config. The file is kept
at chmod 0600 because it carries the bearer token.

Settable keys: server_url, username.
Read-only keys (managed by login/logout): access_token, api_token_id,
refresh_token. Secret values are redacted in every output format.

  astro config [command]

Available Commands:
  current     Show the current config (tokens redacted in table/text)
```

## `astro k8s`

```text
Hands the path off to the management plane's /api/v1/clusters/{id}/k8s/*
endpoint, which forwards it to the managed cluster's apiserver via
the agent WebSocket. The response body is printed verbatim (JSON).

Examples:

  astro k8s <cluster-id> api/v1/namespaces
  astro k8s <cluster-id> apis/apps/v1/namespaces/default/deployments
  astro k8s <cluster-id> apis/aquasecurity.github.io/v1alpha1/vulnerabilityreports

The API path is whatever kubectl would put after "kubectl get --raw=".
Leading slashes are stripped automatically.

Usage:
  astro k8s <cluster-id> <api-path> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for k8s

Global Flags:
      --json            alias for --output json (deprecated)
  -o, --output string   output format: table|json|yaml (default "table")
      --server string   Astronomer server URL (overrides ~/.config/astronomer/config.yaml)
      --token string    API bearer token (overrides stored JWT; ASTRO_API_TOKEN also honored)
```

## `astro login`

```text
login prompts for username + password (or reads them from
--user / --password / $ASTRO_PASSWORD), establishes a cookie-bound browser
session, and exchanges it for a 30-day API token stored in
~/.config/astronomer/config.yaml.

The persisted token is used for every subsequent astro command and is revoked
remotely by astro logout. Browser access and refresh JWTs are never exposed to
the CLI.

Usage:
  astro login [flags]

Examples:
  astro login --server https://astronomer.example.com
  astro login --user admin --password "$(pass astronomer/admin)"
  ASTRO_PASSWORD=… astro login --user admin

Flags:
  -h, --help              help for login
      --password string   password (prompted when omitted; ASTRO_PASSWORD env also honored)
  -s, --server string     Astronomer server URL
  -u, --user string       username (prompted when omitted)

Global Flags:
      --json            alias for --output json (deprecated)
  -o, --output string   output format: table|json|yaml (default "table")
      --token string    API bearer token (overrides stored JWT; ASTRO_API_TOKEN also honored)
```

## `astro nodes`

```text
Inspect and manage the Kubernetes nodes of a registered cluster.

All subcommands take the cluster's UUID as their first argument; the
node-scoped ones also take the node name. Mutating actions (cordon,
uncordon, drain, label, taint, annotate) are proxied to the cluster's
agent and require the operator to have node-management permissions.

Usage:
  astro nodes [command]

Aliases:
  nodes, node

Available Commands:
  annotate        Add or update an annotation on a node
  annotate-remove Remove an annotation from a node
  cordon          Mark a node unschedulable
  drain           Evict pods from a node (cordons first)
  get             Show one node's details
  label           Add or update a label on a node
  label-remove    Remove a label from a node
  list            List the nodes of a cluster
  taint           Add or update a taint on a node
  taint-remove    Remove a taint from a node
  uncordon        Mark a node schedulable again

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for nodes

Global Flags:
      --json            alias for --output json (deprecated)
  -o, --output string   output format: table|json|yaml (default "table")

      --token string    API bearer token (overrides stored JWT; ASTRO_API_TOKEN also honored)

Use "astro nodes [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```
